sources.quote: "12.2 Dakota Accent Rule (DAR): Primary stress is assigned by the Dakota Accent Rule (DAR), as described and motivated in Shaw (1980:31-44). ... The rule states that primary stress is assigned to the second syllable of a word unless there is only one syllable, in which case primary stress is assigned to that syllable. As a consequence of this rule, primary stress never falls beyond the second syllable. Primary stress moves leftwards as prefixes are added to a word." (Cumberland 2005:57)
sources.note: The exact work our deciding quote (p. 57 sec. 12.2) is attributed to; a legitimate copy (ProQuest AAT / Groningen e-book, campus-restricted) is needed to verify the quotation verbatim.
